[[File:Jeri Metzger Mulrow in 2015.jpg|thumb|Mulrow in 2015]]
'''Jeri Metzger Mulrow''' is an American statistician, the 2026 president of the [[American Statistical Association]]. Formerly a government statistician and deputy director at the US [[Bureau of Justice Statistics]], she works as a vice president at [[Westat]], a company that provides data collection and analysis services to the US government and businesses.{{r|ps}}

==Education and career==
Mulrow was born in [[Denver, Colorado]], the daughter of John K. Metzger and Connie Setoo;{{r|cw}} she grew up in [[Helena, Montana]],{{r|ps}} where her mother moved with her second husband, Norman E. Waterman.{{r|cw}} Although she had loved mathematics in school, she entered [[Montana State University]] intending to major in chemical engineering, but quickly switched to mathematics.{{r|sl}} After a 1982 bachelor's degree,{{r|bs}} she received a master's degree in statistics from [[Colorado State University]].{{r|sl|dd}}

She spent the bulk of her career in service to the US government,{{r|ps}} in the [[National Institute for Standards and Technology]], [[Internal Revenue Service]], [[National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics]], and the [[Department of Justice]],{{r|bc}} where she became Principal Deputy Director at the Bureau of Justice Statistics in 2016. Outside the government, she also worked at [[Southern Illinois University]], [[NORC at the University of Chicago]], and [[Ernst & Young]].{{r|dd}} After she retired from the government, she became a vice president at Westat.{{r|bc}}

She was elected as president of the American Statistical Association in 2024, for a one-year term beginning in January 2026.{{r|ep}}

==Recognition==
Mulrow was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2010.{{r|af}} She was one of three 2013 recipients of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]] for distinguished service to the association.{{r|fa}}
